evidence: app/main.py:28: the user-controlled `key = request.args.get("status", "open")` is used only as a dictionary lookup key. app/main.py:29: `status = REPORT_STATUSES.get(key, "OPEN")`. The result is always one of the hardcoded constants defined at app/main.py:8-12 ("OPEN", "SHIPPED", "REFUNDED"), with "OPEN" as the default. app/main.py:31: only that constant is put into the f-string, so attacker input can never reach the SQL text. Nothing else writes to REPORT_STATUSES; it is module-level and only read. Side note: this route has no authentication either (app/main.py:25-26), even though its docstring calls it an operations dashboard. Anyone can see the order counts, but that is not SQL injection.
recommended_fix: No security fix needed for CWE-89. Optional hardening so scanners stop flagging it and it stays safe if the allowlist changes later: `conn.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM orders WHERE status = ?", (status,))`. Separately, decide whether this ops-dashboard endpoint should require authentication.
title: False positive: /reports/status interpolates only allowlisted constant values
